en.title: Impersonal constructions
en.summary: An impersonal construction has a dummy subject such as it or there.

paragraphs: English sentences need a subject. When there is no real subject, English uses a dummy subject: it for weather, time, distance and opinions, and there for existence. These words carry no meaning of their own.

blocks.html:
UseExample
weatherIt is cold. It snows in winter.
time and dateIt is nine o'clock. It is Monday.
distanceIt is ten miles to town.
judgementsIt is important to rest.
opinions and factsIt seems that he is late.
with a clauseIt is a pity that you cannot come.

paragraphs: Use there + be to say that something exists or is present. The verb agrees with the noun that follows: There is a book; There are two books. The same structure works in all tenses: There was; There will be; There has been.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementThere is a bank near here.
questionIs there a bank near here?
negativeThere isn't a bank. / There is no bank.
pluralThere are three students.
pastThere was a storm.

paragraphs: Impersonal passive structures such as It is said that... and It is believed that... avoid naming who says or thinks. In formal writing one can mean any person: One should always be polite. The pronoun you is more usual in everyday speech.

items: Wrong: **Has a problem.** Right: **There is a problem.**
Wrong: **There are a book.** Right: **There is a book.**
Wrong: **It has a lot of people here.** Right: **There are a lot of people here.**
